clue.text: Charged a couple of hundred — taken advantage of

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so two of them give CC
someone taken advantage of has been used

explanation.surface: A man faced with two hundred charges complains he has been exploited.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone charged with a crime stands formally indicted before a court.

clue.text: Youth is grabbed by North- European song-writer

indicators.note: being grabbed by something puts these letters inside the letters of the grabber

parts.note: a Balt is a native of one of the Baltic states in northern Europe
a lad is a youth
taken as written

explanation.surface: A young man is seized by someone from northern Europe who writes songs.
explanation.walkthrough: The Baltic states are Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania; 'grabbed by' signals that the youth and 'is' sit inside the northerner.
explanation.definitionFit: A balladist composes ballads, a narrative kind of song or poem.

clue.text: Leave an area short of water

explanation.surface: Abandon a spot that is running low on water.
explanation.definitionFit: To abandon a post or person is one sense; the other is an arid region with scant rainfall, such as the Sahara.

clue.text: Five battle without a break

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five

indicators.note: used in its old sense of outside, so the letters of battle go around the a

parts.note: action is fighting, as in seeing action in a war

explanation.surface: Only a handful keep fighting without any rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside: ACTION is wrapped round A to give ACATION after V. The page reads 'Few', but nothing in 'few' gives V, so 'Five' is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: A vacation is a holiday, a period of rest away from work or study.

clue.text: This variety of pumpkin grew to be a marvel due to shape

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase before it are given a new shape, that is rearranged

explanation.surface: A gardener boasts that his pumpkin grew into a marvel of form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'due to' is a link; 'shape' is the anagram signal working on all fifteen letters of 'grew to be a marvel'.
explanation.definitionFit: The marrow is a large cucurbit of the same family as squashes and gourds, a British garden staple.

clue.text: Claim sex activity may lead to this

definitions.text: Claim sex activity may lead to this

indicators.note: activity among the letters means they are stirred up into another order

explanation.surface: A suggestive remark about where amorous activity may end up.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: 'activity' stirs the letters of CLAIM SEX.
explanation.definitionFit: Climaxes are high points or culminations, here with a sexual double meaning.

clue.text: Try some relish

explanation.surface: A cook offers a sample of a pickle.
explanation.definitionFit: To sample a little of food is one sense; the other is liking or appetite, as in a taste for adventure.

clue.text: Work in one — forward thinking

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a musical work
I is the Roman numeral one
on means forward, as in moving on

explanation.surface: Someone at work with a progressive outlook.
explanation.definitionFit: Our thinking on a matter is our view or belief about it.

clue.text: Chopped capers to make a pickle

indicators.note: chopping the word up and reassembling it gives a new order of its letters

explanation.surface: A recipe step: cut up capers to make a relish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pickle' looks like the food, but here it is a predicament.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a pickle means being in a fix, a predicament.

clue.text: Profit mentioned, though it's denied

parts.note: gain is profit
something mentioned has been said

explanation.surface: Someone talks about profit, though it is officially disputed.
explanation.definitionFit: Gainsay is a formal verb for contradicting or disputing, so its past tense matches refused or contradicted.

clue.text: Scoring highest is sweet

explanation.surface: Winning at darts deserves a treat.
explanation.walkthrough: A bullseye is also a British hard boiled sweet, striped black and white.
explanation.definitionFit: Hitting the centre of a dartboard or target scores most; the other sense is a striped peppermint candy.

clue.text: Woman cooking A1 meal

indicators.note: cooking the letters mixes them up into a new dish

parts.note: the figure 1 is read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A woman preparing a first-rate dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 is slang for first-rate; the digit 1 stands in for the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Amelia is a female given name.

clue.text: Family conflict to some end

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Family conflict to some end', gives only the definition and END; nothing accounts for V and ETTA, so the clue seems cut short.

clue.text: Increasing strain

explanation.surface: A rising tension.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals multiplying by reproduction are increasing; the other sense is pedigree or lineage, as in good stock.

clue.text: Trifling figure to a syndicate

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500, a figure
an alliance is a syndicate or association

explanation.surface: A small sum offered to a business consortium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link; the Roman numeral D is the figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Dalliance is idle flirtation or toying with something, as in trifling with affections.

clue.text: Scorn tea makers, not being of the modern generation

definitions.text: not being of the modern generation

indicators.note: the letters are made into something new, a signal to rearrange them

explanation.surface: Old-timers who sneer at tea brewers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makers' looks like part of 'tea makers', but it is the anagram signal for SCORN TEA.
explanation.definitionFit: A forebear is someone from whom one descends, belonging to an earlier generation.

clue.text: Condemnation must come to a stop!

explanation.surface: A judge declares that wrongdoing must end.
explanation.definitionFit: A court's punishment imposed on a convict is one sense; the other is a grammatical unit that ends with a full stop.

clue.text: Oriental spur giving rise to strong feeling

parts.note: E is short for east, the Orient
a motive is a spur or incentive

explanation.surface: An Eastern incentive that stirs passions.
explanation.definitionFit: Emotive language arouses passion rather than reason.

clue.text: Sought admittance, but was not at all appreciative

explanation.surface: Someone came to the door and then criticised the host.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapping on a door to be let in is one sense; the other is the informal one of criticising harshly.

clue.text: Way to travel a man holds doubly modish

indicators.note: holding something puts it inside the holder's letters
doubly says the holding happens twice over, so the word for modish goes in at two places

parts.note: a man is a male
in means fashionable or modish
in means fashionable or modish

explanation.surface: A fashionable fellow describes his route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doubly' means the modish word goes in twice, at two separate places, not as one block; 'holds' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A main line is a principal railway route between major towns.

clue.text: Those aiming to make a run if jailed

definitions.text: Those aiming to make a run if jailed

parts.words: Those aiming to make a run if jailed
parts.note: a run here is an escape, which only prisoners locked up would attempt

explanation.surface: Would-be escapees behind bars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make a run' suggests cricket or sport, but it means a dash for freedom.
explanation.definitionFit: Inside is slang for being in prison, where escapers are held.

clue.text: Being a little pest about second cold dish

indicators.note: about means going round, so the letters of a little pest surround the next piece

parts.note: a mouse is a small rodent pest

explanation.surface: A small pest is found near a chilled dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: A mousse is a light whipped dish, sweet or savoury, served chilled.

clue.text: A quarter fly, coming and going

parts.note: S is south, one of the four compass quarters
to wing is to fly

explanation.surface: An insect flitting to and fro.
explanation.definitionFit: A swing moves to and fro, back and forth repeatedly.

clue.text: Fact-finding orders scare her

indicators.note: putting the letters in new orders means rearranging them

explanation.surface: Investigative orders frighten a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'orders' looks like a noun, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Research is systematic investigation to establish facts.

clue.text: Very unpleasant, and that's certainly not right!

explanation.surface: Something nasty that is plainly wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: In heraldry sinister means left, the opposite of right.
explanation.definitionFit: Menacing or evil is one sense; the other is the Latin-derived heraldic sense of left-hand side.

clue.text: Worker taking a cut?

parts.note: to dock is to cut, so one who docks may be read as one taking a cut, though this worker is at the harbour

explanation.surface: An employee pocketing a share.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking a cut' suggests a share of money, but docking is cutting, as in docking a tail.
explanation.definitionFit: A port labourer who loads and unloads ships works at the waterfront.

clue.text: How greed can raise a barrier

indicators.note: the letters can raise or build up something new, a signal to rearrange them

explanation.surface: Avarice leads to fences being put up.
explanation.definitionFit: A row of bushes forms a field boundary in the countryside.
